text:
sarah_pm: quick sync — drafting PRD acceptance criteria for the on-prem hosting network piece. customers keep asking for 'bring your own egress' but we need clear launch gates. main things to decide: customer-managed NAT vs redwood-managed egress, ipv6 support baseline, canary/fallback behavior, and tests for stateful sessions. list below and please thumbs-up or call out gaps.

1) Must-have acceptance checks before GA:
- control plane connectivity: control-plane -> customer-controlplane handshake OK for 3 regions
- config drift tolerance: changes in customer route tables should not drop traffic for >= 5m
- fallback policy: if customer egress fails, traffic routes to our managed egress within 30s and no request loss (best-effort)
- auth & logging: KMS keys validated, audit logs show src/dst IP, and at-rest logs encrypted

2) Edge cases to cover:
- customers using overlapping private CIDRs + NAT hairpinning
- asymmetric routing where return path differs (we need connection tracking validation)
- IPv6-only customer endpoints (do we require dual-stack or allow v4-to-v6 translation?)

3) Tests we can automate for acceptance:
- convo replay: run 10k model requests from customer env and assert 99.9% success within expected latency 95th% <= 500ms
- failover test: bring down customer egress, assert failover completes and no 5xx spikes beyond acceptable window
- route-change blast: update route table and ensure no connection resets for long-lived streams

callout: we need a compact set of knobs in the PRD for product: `egress_mode: customer|redwood|hybrid`, `ipv6: required|optional`, `fallback_timeout_s`

ajay_neteng: +1 to defining `egress_mode`. ops note: if we allow BYO egress we must mandate BGP or static tunnel with health probes. otherwise fallback is brittle. suggest the following minimal network contract:
- BGP session OR GRE/VXLAN with HA pair and health probe endpoint (tcp/443 healthcheck)
- prefix advertisement check: we need an expected prefix list and route origin verification
- heartbeat: customer MUST respond to our control-plane heartbeat within 10s or we consider egress degraded

acceptance test snippet (pseudo):
```
# check BGP session up and advertised prefix present
bgp_peer_up = check_bgp(peer_ip)
advertised = fetch_advertised_prefixes(peer_ip)
assert expected_prefix in advertised
```

maria_dev: couple of implementation questions:
- model-level sessions (kv cache, streaming) depend on source IP preservation. if customer NATs everything to a single IP we might break sticky KV caches. requirement: either preserve original client identity via X-Forwarded-For or provide per-connection session stickiness tokens.

example quick tcpdump to validate source preservation:
```
# on customer edge
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.0.0.5 and port 443 -c 50
```

luke_oncall: also add SLO/alert acceptance: we need a playbook entry and alert runbook before GA. suggested alerting:
- increased 5xx rate > 0.5% for > 1m : page oncall
- failover time > `fallback_timeout_s` : page oncall
- route flaps > 3 in 10m : non-paging alert to eng-platform channel

deploy-bot: automated checklist created: https://intranet.redwood/ops/checklists/onprem-network-acceptance (DO NOT MERGE until all checks pass) :white_check_mark:

ajay_neteng: edge-case: customer uses IPv6-only control plane but v4 model endpoints. I recommend GA require IPv4 for control plane; IPv6 data plane optional (beta). If we push dual-stack at GA we double testing matrix.

sarah_pm: good point. propose we set PRD defaults:
- `egress_mode`: default `hybrid` (prefer customer egress, fall back to redwood-managed)
- `ipv6`: `optional` at GA, `required` for regulated customers only
- `fallback_timeout_s`: 30s default, configurable per customer

final asks: can owners call out who'll own each gate? please reply with owner handle + "owns gate" and any objections. i'll consolidate into the PRD doc.

maria_dev: i'll own the session-preservation acceptance tests — owns gate
ajay_neteng: i own network contract/BGP+health probe gate — owns gate
luke_oncall: i'll own SLO/alerting/runbook — owns gate

sarah_pm: awesome — i'll update PRD and add the automated test checklist. target: internal signoff by EOD Friday. :spiral_calendar:
